Five dimensions in three groups:
  SHIFT-LEFT (blue)   — devops_governance (0–10), artifact_governance (0–10)
  DETECT     (green)  — security_vuln_mgmt (0–10)
  DEFEND     (purple) — identity_secrets (0–10), runtime_protection (0–10)

Pass the normalized DISPLAY values (DIM_*_DISPLAY from the scoring step, each 0–10, rounded to 1 decimal) and the computed SCORE_PCT (0–100). The chart displays each dimension's fill (X.X/10), the risk tier (Establishing/Developing/Proficient/Leading), and three group sub-scores.

Use in the Mythos report immediately after scoring (Step 5b), before authoring Section 2 (Scores by Dimension). Call this first, embed the PNG, then write the score-bar table.

tools.name: harness_adoption_ccm_ai_cost_guide
tools.description:
Return the Maestro AI Cost Analysis playbook — the single source of truth for analysing GenAI / LLM / foundation-model spend on a Harness CCM account. Call this whenever the user asks about AI cost, GenAI spend, Bedrock cost, Claude/LLM token cost, AI/ML cost optimization, prompt caching savings, batch inference savings, Provisioned Throughput, SageMaker Savings Plans, or 'how much are we spending on AI?'. Other playbooks (CUR Analysis Pass 2, the FinOps BVR AI section, the daily check-in) should load this playbook before running any AI/Bedrock cost query.

The playbook covers:
- The Bedrock CUR billing taxonomy: base service vs AWS-native model inference vs third-party foundation-model inference. Critical: third-party models (Claude, Llama, Mistral) bill as separate '(Amazon Bedrock Edition)' products through AWS Marketplace, so filtering by the 'Amazon Bedrock' service AND/OR filter_aws_billing_entity 'AWS' misses the bulk of model inference spend.
- The correct query method (product breakdown, no service filter, all billing entities, post-filter for the '(Amazon Bedrock Edition)' suffix).
- Verified 2026 token pricing (current Opus $5/$25, not legacy $15/$75) and per-model KPIs (verbosity index, cache hit rate, MoM).
- Token counts: report genAIUsageAmount from the GenAI Cost view (group_by genAIUsageType, genAIModel, genAISubProvider, ...); never estimate tokens from spend. Raw values only, no calculated columns (section 8.7).
- Five optimization levers with verified discounts and detection heuristics: Batch Inference (50%), Prompt Caching (~90% off cache reads), Provisioned Throughput (no-commit / 1-month / 6-month only — no 1yr/3yr), SageMaker Savings Plans (1yr/3yr, up to 64%), and model right-sizing/tiering.
- A structured ai_cost output block and a learnings Change Log.

This is a FinOps / cost playbook. It is NOT the Mythos AI-security assessment (harness_adoption_mythos_guide) — do not mix cost analysis with Mythos scoring.

tools.name: harness_adoption_ccm_health_assessment
tools.description: Return the complete Cloud Cost Health Assessment playbook as markdown. Call this whenever the user mentions a NEW Harness CCM customer who has wired in their cloud connectors so cost data is flowing into the default cloud perspectives. The playbook's job is to scan that data, surface trends and gaps, and produce a scored report showing the value of building out the rest of the Harness CCM platform. Critical scoping: TREAT THE ACCOUNT AS IF ONLY THE CLOUD CONNECTORS ARE CONFIGURED. Even if the customer has set up custom perspectives, cost categories, budgets, AutoStopping rules, or Commitment Orchestrator workflows, IGNORE all of it — those are out of scope. The playbook explicitly forbids listing cost_perspective, cost_category, cost_budget, and cost_autostopping_rule; never passes business_mapping_name; and never calls harness_adoption_ccm_budget_health or AutoStopping savings tools. Bootstrap is just whoami + cost_metadata; every subsequent query is scoped to one of the four default perspective IDs returned (defaultAwsPerspectiveId, defaultGcpPerspectiveId, defaultAzurePerspectiveId, defaultClusterPerspectiveId). Existing partial configuration would bias the assessment and becomes part of the rollout plan rather than the analysis. Tone: lead with the customer's own data; mention Harness CCM as the platform that addresses each finding. Soft positioning — no heavy AI-agent framing. The default wedge line is: 'Visibility tells you what your cloud costs. Harness CCM is the platform that does something about it.' The playbook covers: a two-call bootstrap (whoami + cost_metadata); per-default-perspective live queries for six analysis dimensions (Spend Trend 20%, Commitment Coverage 20%, Non-Prod Footprint 20%, Idle+Rightsizing 15%, Allocation 15% diagnostic, Anomaly Exposure 10% diagnostic); the four-layer savings justification framework with measured-vs-benchmark fallback for the recommendations line; current-vs-projected FinOps maturity radar scored from billing-data evidence; a canonical 11-section report structure (no 'What's Configured Today' inventory — out of scope); a drop-in markdown template; persona-specific cover hooks (VP Eng, FinOps Lead, CFO, Cloud Ops, Platform Eng); theme guidance; and a pre-handoff quality checklist that explicitly verifies no out-of-scope queries were issued. After following the playbook, hand the resulting markdown to harness_adoption_reports_render — the URL it returns is the deliverable.

tools.name: harness_adoption_ccm_bvr
tools.description: Return the complete Business Value Review (BVR) playbook as markdown. Call this at the start of any BVR, QBR, quarterly review, or executive report session for an existing Harness CCM customer. The playbook covers the full end-to-end BVR workflow: (1) Pre-BVR data gathering — five steps from bootstrap through chart generation, markdown authoring, and report rendering. (2) BVR report structure — Executive Summary with FinOps Maturity spider chart, seven CCM module deep-dives (Cost Visibility & Allocation, Commitment Orchestration with EC2/RDS gap framing, AutoStopping, Cluster Orchestrator, Asset Governance & Recommendations, FinOps Agent, Savings Accounting & Forecasting), Cross-Cutting Insights (6–10 quantified findings that connect two or more modules — Anomaly × Tag, AI × Commitment, AutoStopping × RI, etc.), Expansion Signals with per-signal agent queries and upsell framing, and a Prioritized Recommendations Matrix that consolidates all findings into one ranked list with action / source / why / owner / $ impact / effort / time-to-impact / risk / validation columns plus Quick Wins and Strategic Bets cross-views. (3) Applied Recommendations Report — a standalone sub-report on YTD user-applied recommendation savings (distinct from governance enforcement savings — see note below). Includes the pagination workaround (3-page fetch with offsets 0/100/200 because start_time_ms/end_time_ms do NOT filter by appliedAt — must filter client-side), YTD dedup + filter logic, aggregations by month/rule/AWS-service/applier, specs for all eight charts (monthly trend, by rule, governance vs EC2 split, by service, annualized savings by applier, items by applier, cost avoidance value-at-risk, open pipeline top-10), report section order, and formatting rules (every monthly figure paired with annualized, tone conventions for metrics tiles and callouts, chart label length limits). (4) Known Issues table — appliedAt filter bug, GOVERNANCE resourceName schema quirk, null applier attribution, recommendationDetails payload size, and AWS No-Service billing artifacts. SAVINGS SOURCE NOTE: For governance enforcement savings (the '$X.XK' figure shown in the Harness CCM Governance UI), use harness_adoption_ccm_governance_savings instead of the pagination approach. The two streams are: (a) governance enforcement savings → harness_adoption_ccm_governance_savings (calls totalRealisedSavingsV2 directly); (b) user-applied recommendation savings → Applied Recommendations Report pagination approach. Both should be reported in a complete BVR. Metabase gov_actual_savings_l30d = $0 does NOT mean zero governance savings — always call harness_adoption_ccm_governance_savings for the authoritative figure. Use this tool (not harness_adoption_ccm_guide) as the primary playbook when the user asks for a BVR, business value review, QBR, or quarterly report. After following the playbook, hand the resulting markdown to harness_adoption_reports_render — the URL it returns is the deliverable.

tools.name: harness_adoption_reports_render
tools.description:
Register a markdown report (BVR, maturity assessment, monthly review, or any Harness-authored doc) with the in-process report renderer and return a live browser URL. By default the URL auto-opens in the user's default browser. The user can switch themes via the sidebar dropdown (harness / modern / glass / kinetic) and click 'Export PDF' to download a paginated PDF. The report is served from the SAME host and port as the MCP server (HTTP mode) or from a dedicated port HARNESS_REPORT_PORT (stdio mode). The directory containing the markdown file is automatically served as the report's web root, so any relative URL in the markdown (`assets/chart.png`, `images/foo.svg`, `inline.png`) Just Works — no separate assets directory to register. Inputs: markdown_path (absolute path to a .md file with YAML frontmatter); base_dir (optional override for the web root); theme (initial theme); id (optional stable slug for a pinned URL); open_in_browser (default true). FRONTMATTER REQUIRED FOR COVER PAGE: A report without YAML frontmatter at the top of the markdown file will render without a title, cover page, or customer branding. Always add frontmatter BEFORE calling this tool — patch the file first if it is missing:
```yaml
---
title: Report Title
customer: Customer Name
date: YYYY-MM-DD
subtitle: Optional subtitle
---
```
Markdown conventions: YAML frontmatter drives the cover page (title, customer, date, subtitle); :::critical / :::success / :::risk / :::action / :::info / :::warning callouts; ::: metrics ...::: grid blocks; standard markdown tables, figures, footnotes.

markdown_path.description: ABSOLUTE path to the markdown file (e.g. '/Users/me/project/reports/acme-bvr.md'). Relative paths are rejected because the MCP server's cwd differs from your workspace. The directory containing this file is served as the report's web root, so any relative image / link URL inside the markdown resolves correctly off disk.

base_dir.description: OPTIONAL absolute path to override the report's web root. Defaults to the directory containing markdown_path. Use this only when the markdown lives somewhere other than the assets it references (e.g. you keep markdown in `reports/` but assets in a sibling `assets/` and don't want to refactor).

theme.description: Initial theme for the preview URL. User can switch themes in the browser after loading. Unknown IDs fall back to 'harness'.

tools.name: harness_adoption_reports_register_pack
tools.description:
Register a customer report pack directory with the server so it survives restarts without requiring HARNESS_REPORT_PACKS_DIR_EXTRA to be set.

Pass the absolute path to either:
  (a) A pack directory — a folder that directly contains `pack.json` (e.g. '/path/to/coles'). The parent directory is registered as the root so the scanner can find the pack alongside any siblings.
  (b) A root directory — a folder that contains one or more pack sub-directories, each with their own `pack.json`.

The registration is persisted to `out/report-packs-registry.json` and takes effect immediately — no server restart needed. The pack's theme is available at `?theme=<pack-theme-id>` straight away.

Use `harness_adoption_ccm_packs` to list all registered packs and verify the new one appears.

pack_path.description: Absolute path to either a pack directory (containing pack.json) or a root directory (containing one or more pack sub-directories). Must be absolute — relative paths are rejected.

tools.name: harness_adoption_reports_pptx
tools.description: Render a registered markdown report as an editable PowerPoint (.pptx) deck. Each Paged.js page in the themed print view becomes one slide — same visual fidelity as the PDF export. Slides are full-bleed images of the rendered pages (not re-authored editable text), so the theme's typography, callouts, and brand look exactly like the PDF. Good for sharing on-brand review decks without having to rebuild the slides by hand in Keynote / PowerPoint. Requires Playwright + Chromium (installed on demand by `pnpm add playwright && npx playwright install chromium`). Inputs: markdown_path (absolute path to the .md, same as the report-render tool); id (optional stable slug); theme; slide_size (16x9 / 4x3 / A4 — A4 matches the Paged.js page aspect most closely and minimises letterboxing).

tools.name: harness_adoption_reports_diagram
tools.description:
Render a Mermaid diagram to an SVG asset and return the markdown image embed.

Always provide `report_path` (absolute path to the .md report file you are authoring) and `diagram_name` (a short slug, e.g. 'pipeline-arch'). The tool will:
  1. Create `{reportDir}/assets/` if it does not exist
  2. Render the diagram server-side to `{reportDir}/assets/{diagram_name}.svg`
  3. Return `markdown_embed` — a `![...](assets/name.svg)` image reference

Paste `markdown_embed` into the report markdown. The SVG renders in all themes (browser, PDF, PPTX, Word).

**Supported types:** flowchart, sequenceDiagram, gantt, gitGraph, pie, block-beta, classDiagram, stateDiagram, erDiagram, mindmap, timeline, quadrantChart, xychart-beta

**Syntax rules** (Mermaid lexer limitations):
- Avoid `_word_` italic patterns, `*`, `<>`, `==`, `\n\n` inside `{{hexagons}}`, and regex/glob syntax inside node labels
- Always use `fill:none` in style overrides — never hardcode light hex fills
- Use `fill:none,stroke:#colour` for subgraph containers

Omit `mermaid_code` to receive a starter template for the chosen `diagram_type`.

Requires Playwright for server-side rendering: `pnpm add playwright && npx playwright install chromium`

diagram_type.description: Type for the starter template (used when mermaid_code is omitted).

caption.description: Optional italic caption shown below the image.

alt_text.description: Alt text for the image. Defaults to diagram_name.

tools.name: harness_adoption_reports_verify
tools.description:
Verify the quality and completeness of a Harness report (markdown source and/or HTML output). Runs the full set of checks from CUR Analysis playbook Steps 9.6, 9.6b, and 9.7, plus additional markdown source quality checks. 

Markdown checks: YAML frontmatter completeness, required section headings (10 sections in order), embedded raw HTML table detection, duplicate KPI metric blocks, invalid callout names, unclosed callout blocks, unfilled placeholders, broken image references, heroStats format, date/filename alignment.

HTML checks (when html_path provided, CUR report type): Scan A — unfilled {{ template tokens; Scan B — skeleton data placeholders ([—], [replace with...], Agent: replace...); template example number detection; Step 9.6b deprecated CSS class names; Step 9.7 structural markers (all 13 section checks including action card count, risk card sev-* modifiers, pillar count, roadmap card count, timebox count).

Cross-file checks: customer name alignment, date alignment, KPI value consistency, AutoStopping account name alignment.

Returns: ok (boolean), counts per status, full findings list with id/status/title/detail/fix per check, and a human-readable summary.

markdown_path.description: ABSOLUTE path to the markdown source file (.md). Required. Relative paths are rejected — the MCP server cwd differs from your workspace.

html_path.description: ABSOLUTE path to the HTML output file (.html). Optional. When provided, enables HTML-specific checks (Scan A/B, CSS classes, structural markers) and cross-file consistency checks. Omit for markdown-only verification.

report_type.description: Report type. 'cur' (default) enables CUR/CACM-specific HTML checks from playbook Steps 9.6, 9.6b, 9.7 — template example numbers, sev-* modifiers, structural markers like hero-strip, kpi-grid, snap-card, action-rank counts, etc. 'generic' runs only universal checks (placeholder scan, deprecated CSS classes, structural presence) without CUR-specific patterns.

  • feature_gauges  — circular progress rings for feature-adoption %
  • opa_donut       — active vs disabled policy-set donut + side legend
  • org_footprint   — diverging bars (workspaces left, pipelines right) + DNA chip
  • priority_matrix — 3-lane recommendation cards (P1/P2/P3) with effort chips
  • bar             — generic horizontal bar chart for any rankable counts
  • monthly_growth  — dual-line cumulative chart of workspaces + pipelines over N months (pair with harness_adoption_iacm_growth)

Each chart_kind has a precise data schema — call this tool with chart_kind first to get the right shape, then fill it from your scan results.

tools.name: harness_adoption_chaos_guide
tools.description:
Return the complete Harness Chaos Engineering agent guide as markdown. Call this at the start of any chaos engineering session to understand all available tools, their workflows, and when to use each one.

Covers four playbooks:
1. Chaos BVR — when and how to generate a Chaos Engineering Business Value Report PDF using harness_adoption_chaos_bvr. Covers the full data pipeline (service utilisation API, experiment run stats, resilience scores), PDF sections, and parameter reference.
2. K8s Onboarding — step-by-step guide for the multi-phase harness_adoption_chaos_onboard workflow: delegate listing, Terraform generation for org/project/connector, infrastructure creation via REST, enabling Chaos v2, and deploying the Service Discovery Agent.
3. Pod API Block Scenario — how to run the 3-phase harness_adoption_chaos_pod_api_block flow to create experiments that intercept API calls from Kubernetes workloads. Includes the 4 mandatory runtime inputs the user must provide and a full example conversation.

tools.name: harness_adoption_chaos_onboard
tools.description:
Multi-step Kubernetes chaos engineering onboarding. Orchestrates Terraform resources and Harness REST APIs to create an Organization, Project, K8s Connector, Infrastructure, enable Chaos v2, and deploy a Service Discovery Agent.

Workflow:
1. Call with NO step to list available delegates.
2. step='create_terraform' — generates Terraform for org, project, k8s connector.
3. step='create_infrastructure' — creates Harness Environment + Infrastructure via REST.
4. step='enable_chaos' — enables Chaos v2 on the infrastructure via REST.
5. step='create_discovery_agent' — appends discovery agent Terraform resource.

Each step returns structured JSON with next_step instructions.

step.description: Which onboarding step to execute. Omit to list delegates. Steps: create_terraform → create_infrastructure → enable_chaos → create_discovery_agent

delegate_selectors.description: Delegate selector names chosen by the user (required for create_terraform)

output_dir.description: Absolute path to write Terraform files (default: ./chaos-onboarding-tf)

chaos_service_account.description: K8s service account for chaos components (enable_chaos)

discovery_service_account.description: K8s service account for discovery agent

tools.name: harness_adoption_chaos_pod_api_block
tools.description:
Create a Pod API Block chaos experiment that intercepts and blocks specific API calls from a Kubernetes workload, simulating downstream API dependency failures.

3-phase interactive flow:
Phase 1: Call with just project_id to list environments.
Phase 2: Add environment_id to list infrastructures.
Phase 3: Add infra_id + all 4 runtime inputs to create the experiment.

The 4 mandatory runtime inputs are: target_workload_namespace, target_workload_names, path_filter, destination_hosts. Always ask the user for these explicitly.

project_id.description: Harness project identifier where the experiment will be created

target_workload_namespace.description: K8s namespace where the target workload runs (MANDATORY user input)

target_workload_names.description: Name of the deployment/workload to disrupt (MANDATORY user input)

path_filter.description: API path to block, e.g. /api/v1/payments (MANDATORY user input)

destination_hosts.description: Destination host whose API calls to block, e.g. payment-svc.default.svc.cluster.local (MANDATORY user input)

tools.name: harness_adoption_chaos_zonal_failure
tools.description:
Create a Zonal Failure chaos experiment (network loss) through a guided selection flow.

Step-by-step interactive flow — call repeatedly, adding one selection each time:
  1. (no args)        → list Organizations; ask the user to pick one
  2. + org_identifier → list Projects in that org; ask the user to pick one
  3. + project_id     → list Environments in that project; ask the user to pick one
  4. + environment_id → list chaos Infrastructures in that environment; ask the user to pick one
  5. + infra_id       → ask the user for the Blast Radius:
        a) Low Blast Radius  → Pod Network Loss  (blast_radius='pod')
        b) High Blast Radius → Node Network Loss (blast_radius='node')
  6. + blast_radius + inputs → create the experiment.

Low (Pod Network Loss) requires: target_namespace, target_workload, node_label.
High (Node Network Loss) requires: node_label.
Always give the node label example: topology.kubernetes.io/zone=us-east-1a

Chaos duration defaults to 5 minutes (300s) for both experiments.
By default the experiment is SAVED only. Pass run_experiment=true to also run it immediately (require explicit user confirmation first for High Blast Radius).

environment_id.description: Environment identifier (omit to list environments in the project)

infra_id.description: Chaos infrastructure identifier (omit to list infrastructures in the environment)

blast_radius.description: Blast radius: 'pod' = Pod Network Loss (low), 'node' = Node Network Loss (high)

run_experiment.description: If true, immediately run the experiment after saving. Defaults to false (save only). For High Blast Radius (node), only set true after explicit user confirmation.

target_namespace.description: [Low/Pod] K8s namespace where the target workload runs (MANDATORY for pod mode)

target_workload.description: [Low/Pod] Name of the deployment/workload to disrupt (MANDATORY for pod mode)

node_label.description: Kubernetes node label selecting the zone/nodes, e.g. topology.kubernetes.io/zone=us-east-1a (MANDATORY for both modes)

chaos_duration.description: Duration of chaos in seconds (default 300 = 5 minutes)

affected_percentage.description: Percentage of pods (pod mode) or nodes (node mode) to affect (1-100)

tools.name: harness_adoption_chaos_bvr
tools.description:
Collect Chaos Engineering BVR data for a given time period and return it as structured JSON. Use this tool to gather the data, then author a markdown report following the chaos BVR format from harness_adoption_chaos_guide, and finally render it with harness_adoption_reports_render.

Returns: account name, license entitlement metrics (secondary entitlement, minimum teams required threshold = secondaryEntitlement/2, license utilisation % from overall/stats API, teams onboarded % vs threshold), summary metrics (total experiment runs, avg monthly experiment runs, services tested, teams onboarded, probe adoption, failure rate), top projects by runs, critical services (deployments with >5 runs in projects with >10 runs), resource type breakdown (Kubernetes/Linux/VM/etc.), and per-project execution analysis (completed/failed/stopped/blocked/timeout counts with failure rate %).

tools.name: harness_adoption_chaos_recommend
tools.description:
Recommend chaos experiments and metrics to monitor based on a parsed architecture diagram.

Accepts a JSON string describing the system's components (nodes) and their dependencies (edges), fetches existing Harness chaos experiments to identify coverage gaps, computes blast radius and SPOF scores from the dependency graph, and returns a prioritized list of recommended chaos experiments with the metrics to watch during each test.

IMPORTANT: This tool expects pre-parsed component JSON, not a raw image. The calling LLM must first analyze the architecture diagram using its native vision capability and extract nodes and edges before calling this tool.

Node types: k8s_workload, external_api, database, message_queue, load_balancer, service_mesh, serverless, cache, node, unknown.
Edge types: sync_call, async_call, reads, writes, streams, proxies.

Fault catalog is sourced from the Harness ChaosHub library (https://developer.harness.io/docs/chaos-engineering/faults/chaos-faults/). Platform-specific faults (AWS, Azure) are only included when the architecture context platform matches.

components.description: JSON string with the extracted architecture components. Shape: {"nodes":[{"id":"svc-a","label":"Service A","type":"k8s_workload","replicas":3}],"edges":[{"from":"svc-a","to":"db","type":"writes"}],"context":{"platform":"kubernetes","env":"production"}}

org_identifier.description: Harness organization identifier (used to fetch existing experiments)

project_identifier.description: Harness project identifier (used to fetch existing experiments)

criticality.description: System criticality level — adjusts recommendation scoring: standard (1×), high (1.5×), critical (2×). Default: high.

focus_areas.description: Restrict recommendations to specific component types. Leave empty to include all component types. Valid values: k8s_workload, external_api, database, message_queue, load_balancer, service_mesh, serverless, cache, node, unknown.

tools.name: harness_adoption_chaos_diagram_server
tools.description:
Start a local web server for uploading architecture diagrams to drive chaos experiment recommendations.

Use this tool BEFORE calling `harness_adoption_chaos_recommend` when the user wants to upload an image (PNG, JPEG, WebP, SVG) of their architecture.

Three actions:
  • action='start'      — Start the upload server and return the browser URL. Tell the user to open the URL and upload their diagram.
  • action='get_upload' — Retrieve the latest uploaded diagram as base64. Use this after the user confirms they have uploaded their diagram. The returned image_data_url can be passed directly to your vision capability for analysis.
  • action='stop'       — Shut down the upload server (optional cleanup).

Recommended flow:
1. Call with action='start' → share the URL with the user
2. User uploads diagram in browser
3. Call with action='get_upload' → analyze image with vision
4. Ask user for org_id and project_id
5. Call harness_adoption_chaos_recommend with the extracted components

Port defaults: 4322 (override with HARNESS_CHAOS_DIAGRAM_PORT env var). Auto-discovers a free port if 4322 is taken (scans up to 4400). Does not conflict with the main MCP server (3000) or report renderer (4321).

action.description: Action to perform: 'start' launches the upload server, 'get_upload' retrieves the last uploaded diagram as base64, 'stop' shuts the server down.

port.description: Override the starting port for the upload server (default: 4322 or HARNESS_CHAOS_DIAGRAM_PORT). Auto-discovers next free port if this one is taken.

tools.name: harness_adoption_chaos_terraform_experiment_templates
tools.description:
Terraform-based Chaos Experiment Template manager. Three-step workflow:

1. LIST_HUBS — discover account-level ChaosHubs; if none exist, offers to generate Terraform to create one.
2. LIST_TEMPLATES — browse available k8s and Linux experiment templates from the ShashankDwivedi/chaos-customer-templates GitHub repository.
3. GENERATE_TERRAFORM — fetch a selected template YAML from GitHub, parse its faults/vertices/probes, and emit a ready-to-apply main.tf using harness_chaos_experiment_template at account level.

Always call list_hubs first, then list_templates, then generate_terraform. The generated .tf files are written to terraform/<subfolder>/main.tf in the workspace.

hub_name.description: [create_hub] Display name for the new ChaosHub (e.g. 'My Custom Hub')

tools.name: harness_adoption_chaos_import_experiment
tools.description:
Import one or more Chaos Experiments from an account-level ChaosHub into one or more projects using Terraform.

Supports multi-select at every step — the user can choose multiple projects and multiple templates; Terraform resources are generated for every (project × template) combination.

Four-step workflow:
1. list_orgs_and_hubs        — Returns numbered orgs and account-level ChaosHubs. Present them as numbered lists so the user can say "1" or "2, 3" instead of typing identifiers.
2. list_projects_and_templates — Returns numbered projects (for the chosen org) and numbered templates (from the chosen hub). User picks one or more projects and one or more templates by number.
3. list_infras               — Returns numbered chaos infrastructures for a given org + project. For multi-project imports, call once per project. User picks one infra per project by number.
4. generate_terraform        — Accepts arrays of project_ids, template_identities, and infra_ids, then writes a single main.tf with one harness_chaos_experiment resource per (project × template) pair.

AGENT INSTRUCTIONS — resolve numbers to identifiers before each call:
• After list_orgs_and_hubs: if the user says "1" map it to organizations[0].identifier / account_level_hubs[0].identity.
• After list_projects_and_templates: map project number → projects[n-1].identifier; template number → templates[n-1].identity.
• After list_infras: map infra number → infrastructures[n-1].infraID.
• For generate_terraform: pass arrays even for single selections.

Import type options to explain to the user:
• LOCAL     — Full copy. You can edit the experiment freely but template changes won't auto-sync.
• REFERENCE — Live link. Template changes auto-sync but the experiment cannot be edited directly.

tools.name: harness_adoption_jira_attach
tools.description: Attach one or more files (Markdown report, PDF, PPTX, PNG chart, MP4, etc.) to an existing Jira issue via the Jira Cloud REST API. Use this whenever the user wants a report pack uploaded to a Jira ticket — the official Jira MCP server does not support file attachments. Provide the issue key (e.g. 'PROJ-123') and either absolute file paths or inline base64-encoded data. Requires ATLASSIAN_EMAIL, ATLASSIAN_API_TOKEN, and ATLASSIAN_BASE_URL to be configured (env or per-session X-Atlassian-* headers).

issue_key.description: Jira issue key (e.g. 'FINOPS-123') or numeric issue id. The issue must already exist; use the official Jira MCP server (or the Jira UI) to create it first.

path.description: ABSOLUTE path to the file to upload (e.g. '/Users/me/report.pdf'). Relative paths are rejected because the MCP server's cwd differs from your workspace. Mutually exclusive with `data`.

data.description: Base64-encoded file contents. Use this when the artefact is in memory and not on disk. Mutually exclusive with `path`. Requires `filename` to be set.

filename.description: Filename Jira will display. Required when using `data`; optional when using `path` (defaults to the basename). Used to infer MIME type when `mime_type` is omitted.

mime_type.description: Optional MIME type override. If omitted, inferred from the filename extension (.pdf → application/pdf, .md → text/markdown, .pptx → …, etc.). Jira will sniff the bytes server-side regardless.

files.description: List of files to attach in a single multipart upload. Each entry must specify either an absolute `path` or base64 `data` + `filename`.

timeout_ms.description: Request timeout in milliseconds. Defaults to 60000 (1 minute). Increase for very large uploads.

annotations.title: Attach files to a Jira issue

tools.name: harness_adoption_jira_download
tools.description: List and optionally download attachments from an existing Jira issue via the Jira Cloud REST API. The official Jira MCP server does not support attachment downloads. Provide the issue key (e.g. 'PROJ-123'). When `output_dir` is supplied (absolute path), each attachment is written to disk; otherwise the tool returns the attachment list (id, filename, mime_type, size_bytes, content_url) for inspection. Filter the set with `attachment_ids` and/or `filename_pattern` (case-insensitive substring). Requires ATLASSIAN_EMAIL, ATLASSIAN_API_TOKEN, and ATLASSIAN_BASE_URL (env or per-session X-Atlassian-* headers).

issue_key.description: Jira issue key (e.g. 'FINOPS-123') or numeric issue id whose attachments to list/download.

output_dir.description: ABSOLUTE directory path where attachment bytes should be written (e.g. '/Users/me/triage/jira-FINOPS-123'). The directory is created if missing. Omit this argument to only list attachment metadata (no file I/O).

attachment_ids.description: Optional whitelist of Jira attachment ids to act on. When omitted, all attachments on the issue are considered (after `filename_pattern` is applied).

filename_pattern.description: Optional case-insensitive substring matched against each attachment filename, e.g. '.pdf' to keep PDF names. Combined with `attachment_ids` (logical AND).

overwrite.description: When true, overwrite files in `output_dir` that already share a name with an attachment. Default false — collisions get a `-1`, `-2`, … suffix to keep prior downloads intact.

include_content_base64.description: When true and `output_dir` is omitted, also include base64-encoded `content_base64` for each (filtered) attachment so the agent can use the bytes inline. Default false. Ignored when `output_dir` is set.

timeout_ms.description: Per-request timeout in milliseconds. Defaults to 30000 for the metadata fetch and 120000 for each download. Increase for very large attachments.

annotations.title: Download files from a Jira issue

tools.name: harness_adoption_markdown_to_pdf

markdown.description: Raw Markdown text to convert. Use this when the content is not on disk. Mutually exclusive with `input_path`.

output_path.description: ABSOLUTE path for the output PDF (e.g. '/Users/me/project/triage/report.pdf'). MUST be absolute — relative paths are rejected because the MCP server's cwd differs from your workspace. Defaults to the input_path with a .pdf extension.

title.description: Title shown in PDF metadata and as a header on the first page.

page_size.description: Page size for the PDF. Defaults to A4.

tools.name: harness_adoption_markdown_to_docx
tools.description: Convert a Markdown file or raw Markdown text to a native editable Word (.docx) document. Provide either input_path (path to a .md file) or markdown (raw text). Headings, lists, tables, blockquotes, code blocks, and inline formatting (bold / italic / code / links) are preserved as live docx structure — not rasterized. The document opens cleanly in Microsoft Word, Google Docs, and Pages. Saved to output_path (defaults to the input path with a .docx extension).

input_path.description: ABSOLUTE path to a Markdown file to convert (e.g. '/Users/me/project/docs/report.md'). MUST be absolute — relative paths are rejected because the MCP server's cwd differs from your workspace. Mutually exclusive with `markdown`.

markdown.description: Raw Markdown text to convert. Use this when the content is not on disk. Mutually exclusive with `input_path`.

output_path.description: ABSOLUTE path for the output .docx (e.g. '/Users/me/project/triage/report.docx'). MUST be absolute — relative paths are rejected because the MCP server's cwd differs from your workspace. Defaults to the input_path with a .docx extension.

title.description: Title shown in docx metadata and as a title paragraph on the first page.

page_size.description: Page size for the document. Defaults to A4.

tools.name: harness_adoption_rules_install
tools.description: Returns the AIM workflow rules and the exact file path where each supported AI client expects them. The calling agent writes the files using its own file tools — this tool only supplies the content and install instructions. Invoke when the user says 'aim: install rules', 'install aim rules', or 'install rules for <client>'.

clients.description: Which clients to generate rule files for. Pass ["all"] to get every supported client. Supported values: cursor, vscode, kiro, claude, agents (AGENTS.md). Defaults to ["all"] when omitted.

tools.name: harness_adoption_setup
tools.description: Run first-time AIM setup. Invoke when the user says 'aim: setup', 'setup aim', or 'set up aim'. Does two things in sequence: (1) Installs AIM workflow rules into the workspace for ONE client — the IDE/agent runtime you are currently running in. Pass `client` matching your runtime: 'cursor' for Cursor, 'vscode' for VS Code Copilot, 'kiro' for AWS Kiro, 'claude' for Claude Code/Desktop, 'agents' for any other runtime that honors AGENTS.md (OpenAI Codex, generic agents, or when unsure). (2) Checks if the Playwright Chromium browser is installed for PDF export and returns the install command if it is not. After getting the result: write the rule files using your file tools, then run the browser_install_command in a terminal if chromium_installed is false.

client.description: Which IDE/agent runtime you are currently running in. Setup writes rule files for this client only — not every supported client. Values: 'cursor' (.cursor/rules/aim-workflow.mdc), 'vscode' (.github/copilot-instructions.md + companion), 'kiro' (.kiro/steering/aim-workflow.md), 'claude' (CLAUDE.md), 'agents' (AGENTS.md — universal fallback for any other runtime). Defaults to 'agents' when omitted.

tools.name: harness_adoption_util_date_range
tools.description: Convert a human-readable date expression into exact epoch millisecond timestamps and ISO date strings required by CCM query tools and any other Harness tools that accept start_time_ms / end_time_ms. ALWAYS call this tool before using custom timestamps — never hand-calculate epoch milliseconds. Supports named presets ('last week', 'this month', 'last 30 days', 'last 7 days', 'yesterday', 'today', 'this quarter', 'this year', 'last month', 'last 14 days', 'last 90 days'), specific date ranges ('June 7 to June 14, 2026', 'June 8 through June 12', '2026-06-07 to 2026-06-14'), relative expressions ('previous 8 days ending June 14'), and single dates ('June 7, 2026', '2026-06-07'). Returns start_time_ms, end_time_ms, start_date (YYYY-MM-DD), end_date, start_utc (human-readable UTC), end_utc, day_count, a human label for report titles, and prior_period (equal-length window immediately before the requested range — use for week-over-week or period-over-period comparisons).

expression.description: Human-readable date expression. Examples: 'June 7 to June 14, 2026', 'last week', 'this month', 'last 30 days', 'previous 8 days ending June 14', '2026-06-07 to 2026-06-14', 'yesterday', 'June 8, 2026'

reference_date.description: Optional ISO date (YYYY-MM-DD) to use as 'today' when resolving relative expressions. Defaults to the actual current UTC date if omitted. Use this when the user says 'last week' and you want to anchor relative to a specific date.

tools.name: harness_adoption_util_timestamp_verify
tools.description: Decode one or more epoch millisecond timestamps into human-readable UTC date/time strings. Use this to verify that a timestamp is correct before passing it to any query tool — especially when hand-calculating timestamps or converting from seconds. Returns the UTC date string, ISO date, day of week, and a sanity flag indicating whether the timestamp falls within a plausible recent range (2024–2028). Accepts a single timestamp or an array of timestamps for batch verification.

anyOf.description: A single epoch millisecond timestamp to verify.
An array of epoch millisecond timestamps to verify in batch.

timestamps_ms.description: One or more epoch millisecond timestamps to decode. Examples: 1749340800000 (check what date this actually is), [1749340800000, 1749686400000] (verify a start/end pair).

tools.name: harness_adoption_cd_guide
tools.description:
Return the complete Harness Continuous Delivery agent guide as markdown. Call this at the start of any CD session to understand all available tools, their workflows, and when to use each one.

Covers four playbooks:
1. CD Guide — tool catalogue, calling conventions, and key insight signals.
2. CD BVR — one-shot BVR data collection and full report authoring guide covering pipeline inventory, maturity distribution, trigger posture, DORA metrics, and Jenkins migration opportunities.
3. Pipeline Maturity — per-pipeline scoring playbook using the complexity_score rubric (0-100), with gap analysis and prioritised recommendations.
4. Deployment Frequency — DORA-style cross-project scorecard playbook with Elite/High/Medium/Low tier classification.

tools.name: harness_adoption_cd_bvr
tools.description:
One-shot CD Business Value Review data collector. Fetches pipeline inventory, analyzes top pipelines for maturity, computes DORA metrics, retrieves the deployment frequency timeseries, and returns a structured JSON payload ready for BVR report authoring.

After calling this tool, author the BVR markdown following the cd-bvr.md playbook from harness_adoption_cd_guide, then render with harness_adoption_reports_render.

tools.name: harness_adoption_cd_pipelines_list
tools.description:
List Harness CD pipelines in a project (paged, filterable). Returns pipeline metadata including name, identifier, stage count, modules, storeType (INLINE | REMOTE for GitOps), last execution status, and 7-day deployment counts.

Key insight signals from this call:
- totalItems → total pipeline count
- GitOps posture: count(storeType=REMOTE) ÷ totalItems
- Activity: pipelines where lastExecutionTs > now-90d
- Last-7d throughput: sum of executionSummaryInfo.deployments arrays
- Distinct stage types: union of stageNames arrays

filter_type.description: Filter type for the pipeline list

tools.name: harness_adoption_cd_pipeline_summary
tools.description: Get summary metadata for a single Harness CD pipeline: name, identifier, stage count, modules, storeType (INLINE | REMOTE), last execution status, and 7-day deployment counts. Does NOT include the YAML — use harness_adoption_cd_pipeline_get for the full YAML.

tools.name: harness_adoption_cd_pipeline_get
tools.description:
Fetch the full Harness CD pipeline including its raw YAML string (yamlPipeline), entity validity details, storeType, and modules.

The yamlPipeline field is the analysis goldmine — it contains deployment types, stage kinds, step kinds, approval gates, failure strategies, environment references, service references, and template usage.

Use harness_adoption_cd_pipeline_analyze to get a pre-parsed structured summary instead of parsing the YAML manually.

tools.name: harness_adoption_cd_pipeline_analyze
tools.description:
Fetch a Harness CD pipeline and return a structured maturity analysis. Parses the yamlPipeline and returns:
- stages[] with per-stage stepKinds, approval flags, failure strategy flags
- stepKindDistribution (which step types are used across the pipeline)
- hasApproval, hasCanary, hasBlueGreen, hasRolling, hasMatrixStrategy, hasTemplateRef, hasFailureStrategy
- envRefs, serviceRefs
- jenkinsWrapperSignals (Jenkins host names detected in ShellScript steps)
- complexity_score (0-100 heuristic) and maturity_band (starter|basic|standard|advanced)
- has_sto, has_scs, has_iacm — stage type presence flags for Mythos scoring
- sto_stage_position — 0-based index of first SecurityTests stage (null if absent)
- scs_sbom — SBOM step detected in SSCA stage
- scanner_names — step types from SecurityTests stages (e.g. Semgrep, AquaTrivy, Bandit)
- notification_configured — notificationRules[] non-empty at pipeline root

Use for BVR maturity distribution, per-pipeline scorecards, Jenkins migration detection, and Mythos Readiness data collection (Section 1 + Section 2 of agent1 spec).

tools.name: harness_adoption_cd_pipeline_validate
tools.description: Validate the YAML of a Harness CD pipeline. Returns entityValidityDetails with valid (bool) and invalidYaml (error string if present). Useful as a pre-check before pipeline maturity reports.

tools.name: harness_adoption_cd_pipeline_variables
tools.description:
Get the resolved variable metadata map for a Harness CD pipeline. Returns every <+...> expression used in the YAML and its resolution context (yamlProperties, yamlOutputProperties, yamlExtraProperties).

Use case: 'what services, connectors, or secrets does this pipeline reference?' without executing it. Walk metadataMap and union unique resource refs in yamlProperties.fqn paths.

tools.name: harness_adoption_cd_pipeline_triggers
tools.description:
List triggers attached to a Harness CD pipeline. Trigger types include: webhook (GitHub/GitLab/Bitbucket/custom), scheduled (cron), artifact (DockerHub/ECR/ACR/Nexus/Artifactory/GCR/S3), and manifest (Helm).

Key insight: pipelines with 0 triggers require a human to click Run for every deployment — this is 'manual deploy debt'. Aggregate across all pipelines to compute trigger adoption %.

tools.name: harness_adoption_cd_pipeline_timeseries
tools.description:
Get daily execution count time series for a Harness project. Returns an array of { date, count } objects suitable for a deployment-frequency line chart.

Feed the output directly into harness_adoption_reports_chart for trend visualization.

pipeline_id.description: Filter by specific pipeline (omit for project-wide)

time_range_days.description: Number of days to look back

tools.name: harness_adoption_cd_pipeline_health
tools.description:
Get health dashboard metrics for a specific Harness CD pipeline over a time window.

Returns executions.total (count + trend vs previous window), success.percent, meanInfo.duration (ms), medianInfo.duration (ms). This is the headline endpoint for CD BVR health sections and per-pipeline scorecards.

tools.name: harness_adoption_cd_executions_list
tools.description:
List pipeline executions in a Harness project (paged). Returns execution status, trigger type (manual/webhook/scheduled/artifact), duration, services deployed, environments, stage results, and failure info.

Use harness_adoption_cd_executions_metrics for pre-aggregated DORA metrics. Use this tool when you need the raw execution objects for detailed analysis.

tools.name: harness_adoption_cd_executions_metrics
tools.description:
Compute DORA-style deployment metrics for a Harness project over a time window. Fetches all executions (up to 500) and returns:
- success_rate_pct
- deployments_total
- deployments_per_day (deployment frequency)
- mean_duration_min
- mttr_hours (mean time to recover — null if no recovery events)
- trigger_breakdown (manual / webhook / scheduled / artifact counts)
- top_pipelines_by_runs (top 5 by execution count)
- top_failure_modes (top status codes other than Success)

Use this for BVR reports and DORA scorecards.

tools.name: harness_adoption_cd_repos_list
tools.description: List distinct Git repositories that have Harness CD pipelines in a project. Useful for computing codebase coverage: compare repo count vs total pipeline count from harness_adoption_cd_pipelines_list to identify concentration (many pipelines from few repos vs broad spread).

tools.name: harness_adoption_cd_filters_list
tools.description: List the customer's saved pipeline or execution filters in a Harness project. These reveal how the team mentally segments their deployments (e.g. 'Production deploys', 'My team', 'Failed last 7 days'). Useful context for CD BVR reports.

tools.name: harness_adoption_governance_opa_check
tools.description:
Check whether OPA (Open Policy Agent) governance policy sets are configured for a Harness project. Returns a boolean `opa_policies_configured` flag and the list of enabled policy sets.

Uses the public policy management API (`GET /pm/api/v1/policysets`), filtered to `type=pipeline` and `action=onrun`. Returns `200` with an empty array when no policies are configured — no 404 handling needed.

Key output fields:
- `opa_policies_configured` — true if any enabled pipeline policy set exists
- `enabled_count` — count of enabled policy sets
- `total_count` — total policy sets including disabled
- `policy_sets[]` — name, identifier, action, enabled status per set

Use for the Mythos Readiness Report Section 6 (Secrets and Governance) and for D5 scoring (`OPA_CONFIGURED` input variable).

include_all_actions.description: If true, fetch policy sets for all actions (onsave, onrun, etc.) instead of onrun only. Default: false (onrun only — the relevant gate action).

tools.name: harness_adoption_secrets_governance
tools.description:
Assess secrets hygiene and governance posture across a Harness project. Scans pipeline YAML for secrets usage patterns and checks service account token expiry configuration.

Component A — Pipeline YAML analysis (public `GET /pipeline/api/pipelines/{id}`):
- `using_secrets_manager` — detects `<+secrets.getValue(...)>` expressions in any pipeline variable, env var, or step config
- `plaintext_values_detected` — flags variables with sensitive names (password, token, api_key, etc.) whose values look like raw credentials
- `suspicious_variable_names[]` — names of flagged variables

Component B — Token rotation (public `GET /ng/api/token/aggregate`):
- `token_rotation_configured` — true if any service account token has an expiry date (`validTo`) set; null if the endpoint returns no tokens
- `tokens_with_expiry` / `tokens_without_expiry` — counts

Use for the Mythos Readiness Report Section 6 (Secrets and Governance) and for D5 scoring (`INFRA_COUNT` secrets component, `TOKEN_ROTATION_OK`).

pipeline_ids.description: Optional list of pipeline identifiers to scan. If omitted, fetches the pipeline list for the project and scans up to 20 pipelines.

max_pipelines.description: Max pipelines to scan when pipeline_ids is not provided. Default: 20.

tools.name: harness_adoption_idp_guide
tools.description:
Return the complete Harness IDP (Internal Developer Portal) agent guide as markdown. Call this at the start of any IDP session to understand all available tools, their calling conventions, and which playbook to follow.

Covers five playbooks:
1. IDP Guide — full tool catalogue, two-account-ID calling conventions, response shape reference (Tier A / UI-only / Backstage proxy).
2. IDP BVR — one-shot BVR data collection and full adoption report authoring covering catalog composition, customization depth, plugin posture, scorecard coverage, self-service activity, ingestion health, and TechDocs freshness.
3. Adoption Health — rapid 6-step decision tree to surface the top 3 IDP gaps using facets, scorecards, home page, plugins, and ingestion health checks.
4. Customization Maturity — 0-100 scoring rubric for home page, layouts, sidenav, custom plugins, and custom catalog kinds.
5. Plugin Recommendations — rule-based engine that maps the currently enabled plugin set to a prioritised list of next plugins to activate.
6. Workflow Candidates — account-wide scan of hand-driven CD pipelines that are strong candidates to become one-click self-service IDP workflows. Use harness_adoption_idp_workflow_candidates to collect data, then author the report following the idp-workflow-candidates.md playbook.

tools.name: harness_adoption_idp_bvr
tools.description:
One-shot IDP Business Value Review data collector. Fetches catalog summary, customization signals, plugin posture, scorecard coverage, workflow activity, catalog completeness analysis (missing owner/lifecycle/description/annotations/relations across all non-template entities), and ingestion health, then returns a structured JSON payload ready for BVR authoring.

After calling this tool, author the BVR markdown following the idp-bvr.md playbook from harness_adoption_idp_guide, then render with harness_adoption_reports_render.

tools.name: harness_adoption_idp_catalog_list
tools.description:
List Harness IDP catalog entities (✅ Tier A public API). Returns entity metadata including kind, type, lifecycle, owner, tags, git_details, scorecard scores, and YAML.

For distribution analytics (counts by kind/lifecycle/owner/tag), prefer harness_adoption_idp_backstage_facets — one call answers group-by questions without iterating entities.

kind.description: Filter by kind(s): component, api, resource, system, domain, group, user, template, aiasset

scope.description: Scope filter — account.* spans all orgs/projects

tools.name: harness_adoption_idp_catalog_get
tools.description: Get a single Harness IDP catalog entity by scope, kind, and identifier (✅ Tier A public API). Returns the same shape as catalog_list items, with the full YAML always populated.

tools.name: harness_adoption_idp_catalog_filters
tools.description: Get available filter facet values for the IDP catalog (✅ Tier A). Returns the actual values present in the data per facet: owner, lifecycle, tags, type. Use when you need 'what tags are even used in this account?' before writing a BVR section.

tools.name: harness_adoption_idp_catalog_kinds
tools.description: List all IDP catalog kinds with their JSON schemas (✅ Tier A). Returns identifier, name, description, icon, and custom flag for each kind. custom=true means the customer defined this kind themselves — a strong customization maturity signal.

tools.name: harness_adoption_idp_catalog_by_refs
tools.description: Bulk-fetch IDP catalog entities by a list of entity refs (✅ Tier A). Returns Harness-flavor entity objects. Use when you have a list of entity_ref strings (e.g. from relation targetRef values) and need their details.
