tools.name: harness_adoption_idp_layout_get
tools.description:
Get the master IDP layout aggregate: per-kind entity-page layouts, sidenav layout, and defaults. ⚠ UI-only gateway endpoint — resilient-parse.

Use the output with harness_adoption_idp_layout_analyze to score customization depth.

tools.name: harness_adoption_idp_layout_get_by_id
tools.description: Get a single IDP layout by its identifier (✅ Tier A — GET /v1/layout/{id}). Use when you know the specific layout identifier (e.g. a plugin layout name).

tools.name: harness_adoption_idp_home_get
tools.description:
Get the IDP home page configuration: header text, quick links, banner, and cards. ⚠ UI-only gateway endpoint — resilient-parse.

Returns a parsed structured object from the home page YAML. Cards section reveals how much the customer has customized their developer home page. Default cards only = no customization. Custom MARKDOWN/CUSTOM_LINK cards = active platform team.

tools.name: harness_adoption_idp_banners_active
tools.description: Get active admin broadcast banners on the IDP home page (✅ Tier A). Active banners reveal current announcements (e.g. 'Jenkins will be retired'). Cross-reference with CD BVR for urgency context.

tools.name: harness_adoption_idp_plugins_list
tools.description:
List all available IDP plugins with their enabled status and category (✅ Tier A — GET /v1/backstage-plugins-info). Returns all ~289 plugins plus computed aggregates:
- enabled_count — total enabled
- enabled_plugins — full objects {id, name, category, plugin_type, custom} for enabled plugins only (replaces the old ID-only array)
- by_category — enabled/total counts per category

Use this as the primary input for harness_adoption_idp_plugins_recommend.

tools.name: harness_adoption_idp_plugins_config
tools.description: Get the effective merged plugin configuration for the IDP account. ⚠ UI-only — resilient-parse. Returns the combined YAML config for all configured plugins (API keys, base URLs, proxy rules).

tools.name: harness_adoption_idp_plugins_custom
tools.description:
List customer-built custom IDP plugins. Uses the Tier A /v1/backstage-plugins-info endpoint and filters to plugin_type=CUSTOM (with a created_by fallback for accounts where plugin_type is absent).

Custom plugins are a strong customization maturity signal — each one represents platform-team investment beyond out-of-the-box Backstage features.

Note: the /gateway/v2/custom-plugins endpoint is attempted first but is known to return empty for some accounts — the tool falls back to filtering the full list.

tools.name: harness_adoption_idp_plugins_recommend
tools.description:
Generate plugin recommendations based on the current IDP plugin state. Fetches plugins and scorecards, then runs a rule engine to produce a prioritised list (P1/P2/P3) of plugins to enable next.

Use as input for BVR plugin posture section and adoption health checks.

tools.name: harness_adoption_idp_scorecards_list
tools.description:
List all IDP scorecards with their checks and overall pass percentage. ⚠ UI-only — resilient-parsed. Returns scorecard name, identifier, published status, entity count, pass %, and check definitions.

0 scorecards = highest-value quick win to call out in any IDP BVR.

tools.name: harness_adoption_idp_checks_list
tools.description: List all IDP scorecard checks (paginated). ⚠ UI-only — resilient-parse. Checks with identifier prefix __HARNESS__ are Harness-shipped; others are customer-authored custom checks.

tools.name: harness_adoption_idp_data_sources_list
tools.description: List available IDP scorecard data sources. ⚠ UI-only — resilient-parse. Typical sources: bitbucket, catalog, github, gitlab, harness, jira, kubernetes, pagerduty.

tools.name: harness_adoption_idp_workflows_history
tools.description:
List recent IDP workflow (scaffolder) execution history. ⚠ UI-only listing — resilient-parse. Returns workflow_name, execution_id, status, executed_at, executed_by, scope, source.

For per-execution detail (step trace), use harness_adoption_idp_backstage_task_get.

tools.name: harness_adoption_idp_workflow_candidates
tools.description:
Scan Harness CD pipeline executions account-wide to surface hand-driven pipelines that are strong candidates to become self-service IDP workflows.

The tool:
1. Lists all orgs and projects in the account.
2. Fetches 30-day execution summaries for every project.
3. Groups executions by pipeline and filters for those where the dominant    trigger type is MANUAL and execution count is above the threshold.
4. Checks whether each candidate pipeline has any automated triggers configured.
5. Returns a ranked list of candidates with run counts, operator names,    abort signals, and a suggested IDP workflow name + form fields.

After calling this tool, author the report following the idp-workflow-candidates.md playbook from harness_adoption_idp_guide, then render with harness_adoption_reports_render.

min_manual_runs.description: Minimum manual run count in the period to qualify as a candidate (default 5)

max_projects.description: Maximum number of projects to scan (most-recently-active first, default 80)

include_ci.description: Include CI pipelines (not just CD) in the manual-run scan

concurrency.description: Number of projects to scan in parallel (default 5, max 20)

tools.name: harness_adoption_idp_workflow_categorize
tools.description:
Fetch all IDP workflow entities and categorize them by use-case using the
Harness v1/entities/groups and v1/catalog/entities APIs. Analyzes workflow name,
description, tags, and spec to classify each workflow into one of six categories:

  a) Scaffolding Service    — workflows that create/bootstrap services, repos, or catalog entities.
                              Detected by: CookieCutter, CreateRepo, DirectPush, GitClone step types;
                              trigger:harness-custom-pipeline action; registeredCatalogEntity /
                              repositoryUrl output vars; service_name / cookie_cutter_repo parameters;
                              OwnerPicker / HarnessProjectPicker UI fields; catalog-info.yaml / idp.yaml
                              file references; or name/description keywords (scaffold, microservice, etc.)
  b) Just In Time Access    — workflows that grant temporary/JIT access, privileges, or IAM roles
  c) Employee Onboarding    — workflows for new hires, user provisioning, or account setup
  d) Ephemeral Environments — workflows that spin up / tear down short-lived environments
  e) Infrastructure Provisioning — workflows that create/manage cloud infra (RDS, EKS, EC2, namespaces)
  f) Other                  — workflows that don't match any of the above categories

Optionally cross-references with execution history to show how many times each
category was executed in the last N days.

include_execution_stats.description: Cross-reference with execution history to add execution counts per category (default: true)

days.description: Look-back window in days for execution stats (default: 30)

scope.description: Scope filter for the catalog query (default: account.*)

include_workflow_list.description: Include per-workflow details in each category (default: true)

tools.name: harness_adoption_idp_backstage_facets
tools.description:
Get group-by analytics for the IDP catalog in one call (🔵 Backstage standard). Returns value-count distributions for any entity field path.

This is the highest-leverage IDP tool — call it FIRST for any catalog analysis:
- kind distribution: facets=['kind']
- lifecycle mix: facets=['spec.lifecycle']
- owner distribution: facets=['spec.owner']
- tag frequency: facets=['metadata.tags']
- type distribution: facets=['spec.type']

Eliminates the need to fetch and count 1000+ entities manually.

Requires HARNESS_IDP_ACCOUNT_ID to be set.

tools.name: harness_adoption_idp_backstage_entities_query
tools.description:
Scan IDP catalog entities with cursor-based pagination and field selection (🔵 Backstage standard — GET /catalog/entities/by-query). Better than harness_adoption_idp_catalog_list for large catalogs because it handles arbitrary sizes cleanly without offset limits.

Requires HARNESS_IDP_ACCOUNT_ID.

cursor.description: Pagination cursor from previous response pageInfo.nextCursor

tools.name: harness_adoption_idp_backstage_entities_by_refs
tools.description: Bulk-fetch IDP entities by ref list in Backstage shape (🔵 Backstage standard — POST /catalog/entities/by-refs). Returns full apiVersion/kind/metadata/spec/relations objects. Use when you need the Backstage shape (e.g. to walk relations). Requires HARNESS_IDP_ACCOUNT_ID.

annotations.title: IDP — Backstage Bulk Entities by Refs

tools.name: harness_adoption_idp_backstage_entity_get
tools.description: Get a single IDP entity in Backstage shape (🔵 Backstage standard). Returns full apiVersion/kind/metadata/spec/relations. Requires HARNESS_IDP_ACCOUNT_ID.

tools.name: harness_adoption_idp_backstage_ancestry
tools.description: Walk the partOf relations hierarchy for an IDP entity (🔵 Backstage standard). Returns rootEntityRef and items[] with entity + parentEntityRefs. Use to understand which system or domain a component belongs to. Requires HARNESS_IDP_ACCOUNT_ID.

tools.name: harness_adoption_idp_backstage_locations
tools.description: List registered catalog source locations (🔵 Backstage standard). Returns id, type, target (Git URL to catalog-info.yaml). Use to compute 'how many distinct repos feed the catalog'. Requires HARNESS_IDP_ACCOUNT_ID.

tools.name: harness_adoption_idp_backstage_health_failed
tools.description:
Get failed ingestion entities from the IDP catalog (🔵 Backstage standard). Returns entities that failed to process, grouped by error type. Failed entities are a P1 health issue — they mean catalog entries are broken.

Requires HARNESS_IDP_ACCOUNT_ID.

tools.name: harness_adoption_idp_backstage_template_schema
tools.description:
Get the JSON schema (input contract) for an IDP scaffolder workflow template (🔵 Backstage standard). Returns the form steps with required fields, types, and UI widgets.

Key insight: templates with >15 required fields create onboarding friction. 3-5 required fields is well-designed self-service.

Requires HARNESS_IDP_ACCOUNT_ID.

tools.name: harness_adoption_idp_backstage_actions_list
tools.description:
List available IDP scaffolder action types (🔵 Backstage standard). Examples: publish:github, fetch:template, harness:create-pipeline, aws:cloudformation:deploy, custom actions.

A customer with only 2-3 basic actions has minimal self-service. One with 30+ actions including custom ones is mature.

Requires HARNESS_IDP_ACCOUNT_ID.

tools.name: harness_adoption_idp_backstage_task_get
tools.description:
Get the full step-by-step execution trace for a scaffolder task (🔵 Backstage standard). Use this to understand why a workflow succeeded or failed.

Get the task ID from harness_adoption_idp_workflows_history.

Requires HARNESS_IDP_ACCOUNT_ID.

tools.name: harness_adoption_idp_backstage_techdocs_metadata
tools.description:
Get TechDocs build metadata for an IDP entity (🔵 Backstage standard). Returns site_name, site_description, etag (git sha), and build_timestamp.

build_timestamp is the docs freshness signal — docs older than 90 days are stale. Use to compute TechDocs coverage and freshness distribution.

Requires HARNESS_IDP_ACCOUNT_ID.

tools.name: harness_adoption_idp_backstage_search
tools.description:
Cross-catalog full-text search across IDP entities and TechDocs (🔵 Backstage standard). Use to 'find anything mentioning X' rather than iterating entities.

Requires HARNESS_IDP_ACCOUNT_ID.

tools.name: harness_adoption_sto_guide
tools.description:
Return the complete Harness STO (Security Testing Orchestration) agent guide as markdown. Call this at the start of any STO session to understand all available tools, their workflows, and when to use each one.

Covers the STO BVR playbook: how to collect security scan data with `harness_adoption_sto_scan`, author a security posture report, generate severity charts and a scorecard, and render the final report. Includes callout rules, metric tone rules, scanner coverage guidance, and zero-data handling for accounts that have not yet configured STO pipeline stages.

tools.name: harness_adoption_sto_scan
tools.description:
Collect Harness STO (Security Testing Orchestration) security posture data across ALL STO-enabled projects in the account and return it as structured JSON.

For each STO project the tool calls (HAR-validated v2 APIs):
- `all-issues/v2/counts?statuses=Active` — severity breakdown (Critical/High/Medium/Low/Info) and issue-type breakdown (SCA, SAST, IAC, SECRET, DAST …)
- `all-issues/v2/counts/total` — total unique issues + raw occurrence count
- `all-issues/v2/trend?intervalDays=30` — daily active-issue trend for the last 30 days
- `all-issues/filters` — scanner coverage (which scan tools and target types are in use)
- `products` — all registered scanner products for the account

Results are aggregated across every STO project in the account. If `org_id` and/or `project_id` are supplied, the tool is scoped to that single org or project.

For accounts with many orgs, use `harness_adoption_orgs_projects(mode="orgs")` first to enumerate all org identifiers, then call this tool once per org.

After collecting data, call `harness_adoption_sto_guide` to load the STO BVR playbook, then author the markdown report and render it with `harness_adoption_reports_render`.

org_id.description: Limit to a specific Harness org identifier. Omit to scan all orgs.

project_id.description: Limit to a single project (requires org_id). Omit to scan all STO projects.

max_projects.description: Maximum number of STO projects to aggregate. Default: 500 (effectively all projects). Lower this only if you want to limit the scan scope intentionally. Previously capped at 50 — that limit is removed; use org_id to scope by org instead.

trend_interval_days.description: Number of days for the active-issue trend. Default: 30.

tools.name: harness_adoption_sto_all_issues_counts
tools.description:
Return project-level severity and issue-type counts for all active STO findings across all baseline scans (not execution-scoped). This is the primary source of account-level security posture data for the BVR.

Calls two HAR-validated endpoints:
1. `all-issues/v2/counts?statuses=Active` — `severityCounts` (critical/high/medium/low/info) and `issueTypeCounts` (SCA, SAST, IAC, SECRET, DAST, CODE_SMELLS, EXTERNAL_POLICY …)
2. `all-issues/v2/counts/total` — `totalIssues` (unique deduplicated) and `totalOccurrences` (raw scanner findings before dedup)

Also returns `all-issues/filters` (`latestBaselineScans`) for scanner coverage.

Example (Platform_Engineering project, HAR 2026-06-11):
- Total: 1,710 unique issues from 458,941 occurrences
- Severity: 192 Critical, 575 High, 781 Medium, 130 Low, 28 Info
- Types: SCA=1192, SAST=240, IAC=198, SECRET=46, DAST=8

statuses.description: Comma-separated status filter. Default: 'Active'. Options: Active, Exempted, Remediated.

tools.name: harness_adoption_sto_all_issues_trend
tools.description:
Return the daily active and remediated issue trend for a project across all baseline scans (not execution-scoped). Use for the 30/90-day security trajectory chart in the BVR.

Returns `trend[]` — one entry per day:
- `date` — ISO date string (YYYY-MM-DD)
- `active` — count of active issues on that day
- `remediated` — count of remediated issues on that day

Query param `intervalDays` controls the window (default 30, max 90).

Example (Platform_Engineering, 30 days): active grew from 1,644 to 1,710 — net +66 new issues introduced over the review period.

interval_days.description: Trend window in days. Default: 30. Max: 90.

tools.name: harness_adoption_sto_all_issues_list
tools.description:
List all active STO security issues across all baseline scans for a project (not execution-scoped). Paginated.

Returns `issues[]` — each entry contains:
- `id`, `title`, `severityCode`, `issueType`, `status`
- `numOccurrences` — total raw occurrence count (blast radius)
- `numTargetsImpacted` — number of distinct targets affected
- `lastDetected` — Unix timestamp of most recent detection
- `exemptionStatus` — Pending | Approved | null

Use for identifying the top critical/high findings to highlight in the BVR. Then pass a specific `issue_id` to `harness_adoption_sto_issue_detail` for full detail.

severity_codes.description: Comma-separated severity filter, e.g. 'Critical,High'. Omit for all severities.

issue_types.description: Comma-separated issue type filter, e.g. 'SCA,SAST'. Omit for all types.

tools.name: harness_adoption_sto_overview_baselines
tools.description:
Return all pipeline execution IDs that have baseline STO scan data for a project. This is the source for the execution list shown on the STO Overview page.

Returns `executionIds[]` — one entry per execution that ran at least one STO scan step and produced a baseline. Pass each ID to `harness_adoption_sto_execution_issues` for detailed per-execution data, or use the execution IDs as a batch input to understand scan volume and coverage.

Example (Platform_Engineering): 20 execution IDs returned, meaning 20 pipeline runs have contributed to the current security baseline.

tools.name: harness_adoption_sto_execution_issues
tools.description:
Collect all STO security data for a specific pipeline execution: issue counts (new vs. existing vs. remediated), deduplication rate, scanner steps, and expiring exemptions. This is the primary data tool for the STO BVR workflow.

Returns:
- `counts` — new/existing/remediated issue counts by severity, `totalDeduplicationRate`, `totalNumOccurrence` (raw occurrence count before dedup)
- `steps` — scanner tools, sub-products, and target types used in this execution; `reachabilityFlag` / `exploitabilityFlag` feature status
- `issues` — flattened list of new + existing issues, sorted by severity float desc
- `expiring_exemptions` — exemptions expiring within `expiry_days` days
- `capability_signals` — pre-computed signals for the 11-capability HAR adoption matrix

After collecting data, call `harness_adoption_sto_guide` to load the playbook, then author the markdown report and render it with `harness_adoption_reports_render`.

execution_id.description: Pipeline plan execution ID (`planExecutionId` from the CD executions list).

include_exempted.description: Include exempted issues in results. Default: false.

page_size.description: Page size for issue lists. Default: 20.

expiry_days.description: Lookahead window in days for expiring exemptions. Default: 30.

tools.name: harness_adoption_sto_execution_steps
tools.description:
List all scanner steps (scan tools, sub-products, and scan targets) that ran in a specific pipeline execution, plus account-level feature flags for reachability analysis and EPSS exploitability scoring.

Returns:
- `steps[]` — one entry per scan step: `scanId`, `scanTool`, `scanToolName`, `subproduct`, `targetName`, `targetType`, `stageId`, `stepId`
- `reachabilityFlag` — true if reachability analysis is enabled for this account
- `exploitabilityFlag` — true if EPSS exploitability scoring is enabled

Use `scanId` from a step to call `harness_adoption_sto_issue_detail`.

tools.name: harness_adoption_sto_expiring_exemptions
tools.description:
List security issue exemptions that will expire within a given number of days for a specific pipeline execution. Use this to surface risk acceptance windows that are about to lapse and require review.

Returns `issues[]` — each exemption includes the issue ID, title, severity, expiry date, scope, and approval status. An empty array means no exemptions are expiring in the requested window.

days.description: Lookahead window in days. Default: 30. Use 7 for near-term alerts.

tools.name: harness_adoption_sto_issue_detail
tools.description:
Fetch full detail for a specific STO security issue, including all raw occurrences, file locations, git repository metadata, fix availability, EPSS exploitability scores, and Harness AI remediation augmentation fields.

Key returned fields:
- `title`, `severity`, `severityCode`, `issueType`, `subproduct`
- `details.fixAvailable` — whether an automated fix exists
- `details.fileName` + `details.lineNumber` — exact source location
- `details.remediationSteps` — remediation guidance from the scanner
- `gitMetadata` — repository path, branch, and Harness git correlation
- `harnessAiAugmentation` — AI-generated remediation code (if enabled)
- `occurrences[]` — all raw occurrence objects with per-location detail

Obtain `scan_id` from `harness_adoption_sto_execution_steps` and `issue_id` from `harness_adoption_sto_execution_issues`.

scan_id.description: Scan ID from the pipeline-security/steps response.

issue_id.description: Issue ID from the pipeline-security/issues response.

page.description: Page index for occurrence pagination. Default: 0.

page_size.description: Page size for occurrence pagination. Default: 20.

tools.name: harness_adoption_sto_products_list
tools.description:
List all enabled scanner products (tools) registered for this Harness account. Returns each scanner's `id`, `name`, `prettyName`, `isEnabled`, and timestamps.

The `id` field on each product matches the `productId` field on STO issue detail objects — enabling joins between scanner registry and issue data.

Use this to understand scanner coverage breadth for the BVR scanner coverage section, or to filter by a specific scanner name.

name.description: Optional scanner name filter, e.g. 'wiz', 'semgrep'. Omit to list all.

tools.name: harness_adoption_sto_dashboard_list
tools.description:
List all Harness STO Looker dashboards available for this account. Returns dashboard IDs, titles, type (SHARED/ACCOUNT), and access metadata.

Known STO dashboards (HAR-validated 2026-06-11):
- **54979** — Security Testing Dashboard (account-level posture across all baselines)
- **54980** — STO Usage Dashboard (scan volume trend over time)
- **58163** — STO All Occurrences (raw occurrence-level export from latest baseline)
- **56671** — STO Pipeline Execution Summary

Use the returned `id` to build dashboard deep-link URLs:
`https://app.harness.io/ng/account/{accountId}/dashboards/detail/{id}`

tools.name: harness_adoption_sto_policy_evaluations
tools.description:
Fetch OPA policy gate evaluation results for STO scan steps. Each evaluation records the severity output variables (CRITICAL, HIGH, NEW_CRITICAL, etc.), external policy failures, and overall gate status (pass/warning/error).

Use this to confirm OPA policy gates are active and to detect whether they fired (status 'warning' or 'error') in recent executions.

Key fields per evaluation:
- `status` — 'pass' | 'warning' | 'error'
- `input[].outcome.outputVariables` — CRITICAL, HIGH, NEW_CRITICAL, NEW_HIGH, EXTERNAL_POLICY_FAILURES, JOB_ID (= scanId), JOB_STATUS
- `entity_metadata` — URL-encoded JSON with executionIdentifier and scanner name

Decode `entity_metadata` with `decodeURIComponent(JSON.parse(...))` to get the scanner name and execution link.

include_child_scopes.description: Include evaluations from child scopes. Default: true.

tools.name: harness_adoption_sto_ticket_settings
tools.description:
Fetch the Jira or ServiceNow ticket integration settings configured for STO in a Harness project. Returns the connector ID, issue type, Jira project key, and the severity threshold for automatic ticket creation.

Key fields:
- `service` — 'Jira' | 'ServiceNow' | null (null = no integration configured)
- `connectorId` — Harness connector reference for the ticket system
- `additional.baselineJiraAutoCreateForSeverities` — 'NONE' | 'CRITICAL' | 'CRITICAL,HIGH'
- `additional.issueType` — Jira issue type (e.g. 'Bug')
- `additional.projectKey` — Jira project key

Use this for the Governance & Compliance section of the BVR rubric — a non-null `service` and non-'NONE' auto-create severity confirms ticket workflow is active.

tools.name: harness_adoption_sto_exemption_detail
tools.description:
Fetch full lifecycle detail for a single STO security issue exemption record.

Returns:
- `status` — full lifecycle: Pending | Approved | Rejected | Canceled | Expired
- `type` — exemption justification category (e.g. 'Compensating Controls')
- `scope` — ACCOUNT | ORG | PROJECT — approval scope level
- `pendingChanges.durationDays` — risk acceptance window in days
- `canApproveFor` — RBAC: which scope levels the current user can approve
- `reason` + `link` — justification text and evidence URL
- `requesterId` — user who created the exemption request

Use this for the Exemption Workflow / RBAC section of the BVR rubric.

tools.name: harness_adoption_sto_issue_occurrences
tools.description:
Fetch the paginated list of all raw occurrences for a specific STO security issue, including full CVE/vulnerability detail for SCA issues.

Use this to analyse blast radius — the number of distinct locations (files, containers, or configuration items) affected by a single logical issue.

Key fields per occurrence:
- `fileName` + `lineNumber` — exact location in the scanned artifact
- `_raw._rawVulnerabilityWithRemediation` — CVE detail for SCA issues: baseScore, cweId, exploitabilitySubscore, impactSubscore
- `severityCode` + `harnessAiAugmentation` — per-occurrence severity and AI remediation

`numNonExemptedOccurrences` shows active exposure after risk acceptance.

scan_id.description: Scan ID from the pipeline-security/steps response.

issue_id.description: Issue ID from the pipeline-security/issues response.

tools.name: harness_adoption_sto_pr_action
tools.description:
Check whether an auto-fix pull request can be raised for a specific STO issue occurrence in a repository.

Returns:
- `action` — 'none' | 'create' | 'view'
  - 'create' = auto-fix PR can be raised (capability is active)
  - 'view' = a PR already exists for this occurrence
  - 'none' = auto-fix not available (check `disabledReason`)
- `disabledReason` — explanation when action is 'none'

Use this for the Auto PR / Code Suggestion rubric capability check. If `action === 'create'` for any issue → the capability is enabled.

issue_id.description: Issue ID from the pipeline-security/issues response.

occurrence_id.description: Occurrence internal ID from the issues or occurrences response.

repository_id.description: Repository target ID from the steps response (`targetId`).

tools.name: harness_adoption_sto_occurrence_dataflow
tools.description:
Fetch the SAST taint-propagation dataflow trace for a specific issue occurrence. Only applicable to SAST findings — returns `hasDataflow: false` for IaC, Secret, and SCA issue types.

When `hasDataflow: true`, the response contains the full taint-propagation path showing how data flows from a source to a vulnerable sink.

Returns:
- `occurrenceInternalId` — the occurrence ID
- `hasDataflow` — whether a SAST data-flow trace is available
- `dataflow` — the taint-propagation path steps (if hasDataflow is true)

issue_id.description: Issue ID from the pipeline-security/issues response.

tools.name: harness_adoption_sto_template_detail
tools.description:
Fetch the YAML and configuration of a named Harness scan step-group template. Use this to understand the scanner strategy standardised at account or project level and assess scanner hygiene for the BVR.

The `template_id` is derived from `matchingSteps[].stepId` in the execution issues response — the step ID encodes the template name as a prefix:
`<templateIdentifier>_<stageId>_<stepName>`

Returns:
- `name`, `identifier`, `templateEntityType` (typically 'StepGroup')
- `yaml` — the full pipeline v0 YAML string of the template
- `versionLabel`, `stableTemplate`, `tags`

BVR value:
- Reveals custom/SARIF scanner configurations (rubric: Scanner Flexibility)
- Shows Wiz policy tier (platinum/gold/silver) if configured
- Enables scanner standardisation assessment across projects

template_id.description: Template identifier (e.g. 'TU_SEAL_IAC_Scan_Templates'). Derived from matchingSteps[].stepId prefix.

version_label.description: Template version label (e.g. 'v1.0.5'). Omit to retrieve the stable version.

org_id.description: Org identifier. Omit for account-level templates.

project_id.description: Project identifier. Omit for account-level templates. Requires org_id.

branch.description: Git branch where the template YAML lives. Omit to use the default branch.

tools.name: harness_adoption_fme_guide
tools.description:
Return the complete Harness FME (Feature Management & Experimentation) agent guide as markdown. Call this at the start of any FME session to understand all available tools, their workflows, and the BVR report format.

Covers:
1. FME BVR — how to generate a Feature Management Business Value Review using harness_adoption_fme_bvr. Covers environment discovery, the five value use cases (progressive delivery, targeted rollout, controlled rollback / kill switch, flag hygiene, decoupled release), ROI slide templates, and the full report format.

Trigger this guide when the user mentions: feature flags, FME, feature management, flag health, flag portfolio, progressive delivery, gradual rollout, kill switch, flag cleanup, FME BVR, feature flag ROI, or Split.

tools.name: harness_adoption_fme_bvr
tools.description:
Collect Harness FME (Feature Management & Experimentation) BVR data and return structured JSON. Use this data to author a markdown report following the FME BVR playbook from harness_adoption_fme_guide, then render with harness_adoption_reports_render.

Three analysis depths (set analysis_depth):
  gallery — gallery cards + env parity (Level 1, fastest)
  sample  — gallery + 200-flag definition sample + use-case classification (default, Level 2)
  full    — sample + workspace-wide rollout lifecycle (paginate up to max_workspace_flags) + tag audit + traffic types (Level 3)

Accepts scope in three ways (use whichever you have):
  1. fme_url — paste any Harness FME URL and all IDs are auto-extracted
  2. harness_org_id + harness_project_id — Harness org/project slugs (e.g. 'BoxIncFME'/'Box_1')
  3. fme_org_id — the raw FME organization UUID

Environment IDs are optional — the tool attempts auto-discovery. If discovery fails, the error response includes a copy-paste-ready URL pattern to retrieve them.

Returns: per-environment flag counts, five value use case breakdowns (progressive delivery, targeted rollout, controlled rollback, flag hygiene, decoupled release), production flag sample, and ROI-ready summary metrics. When analysis_depth='full', also returns rollout_lifecycle.chart_data (pre-built bar chart spec for harness_adoption_ccm_chart), tag_audit, and traffic_type_summary.

fme_url.description: Any Harness FME URL — workspace, environment, flag, or mywork page. All IDs are auto-extracted. Example: https://app.harness.io/ng/account/{acct}/module/fme/orgs/{org}/projects/{proj}/org/{fmeOrgUUID}/ws/{wsUUID}/mywork

harness_org_id.description: Harness organization identifier (slug), e.g. 'BoxIncFME'. Use with harness_project_id to auto-resolve FME workspace.

harness_project_id.description: Harness project identifier, e.g. 'Box_1'. Use with harness_org_id.

fme_org_id.description: FME Organization UUID. Found in the Harness FME URL after /org/. Use this if you already have the UUID.

workspace_id.description: FME Workspace UUID (found in the URL after /ws/). Providing this improves environment auto-discovery.

production_env_id.description: Production environment UUID (optional — auto-discovered if omitted). Found in .../environments/<UUID> in the FME UI URL.

flag_sample_limit.description: Max production flags to sample for use-case analysis (default 200, max 500). Prefer max_production_flags for new callers.

max_production_flags.description: Maximum production flags to scan for value use-case classification (progressive delivery, targeted rollout, etc.). Tiered auto-defaults: 200 for sample depth; 500 for full depth (sampled definitions tier — accurate percentages at lower cost). Override to a higher value (up to 5000) when exact absolute counts are required for large workspaces.

analysis_depth.description:
Analysis depth:
  gallery — gallery cards + env parity only (fast, Level 1)
  sample  — gallery + 200-flag definition sample + use-case classification (default, Level 2)
  full    — sample + workspace-wide rollout lifecycle + tag audit + traffic summary via BFF pagination (Level 3)
Use 'full' for a complete BVR with rollout_lifecycle.chart_data ready for harness_adoption_ccm_chart.

max_workspace_flags.description: Maximum flags to paginate from BFF for rollout lifecycle aggregation when analysis_depth='full'. Auto-defaults to 3000 when analysis_depth='full' (full lifecycle tier) — set explicitly to override. Default 500 for other depths.

tools.name: harness_adoption_fme_resolve_scope
tools.description:
Parse any Harness FME URL or Harness org/project combination and return all FME identifiers (account, org, project, FME org UUID, workspace UUID, environment UUID) as structured JSON. Also discovers environments via the FME BFF when an FME org UUID is available.

Use this tool whenever:
- The user pastes an FME URL and you need the env/workspace/org UUIDs
- You need to convert a Harness org+project slug to FME internal UUIDs
- harness_adoption_fme_bvr needs env IDs but the user only has a URL

Accepts: a full Harness FME URL, OR harness_org_id + harness_project_id, OR a bare UUID (FME org, workspace, or environment).

url.description: Any Harness FME URL — workspace URL, environment URL, flag URL, or the full app.harness.io/ng/account/.../module/fme/... URL.

harness_org_id.description: Harness org identifier (slug), e.g. 'BoxIncFME'. Use with harness_project_id.

harness_project_id.description: Harness project identifier, e.g. 'Box_1'. Use with harness_org_id.

fme_org_id.description: FME org UUID (if already known). Enables direct workspace + environment lookup.

tools.name: harness_adoption_fme_flags_list
tools.description:
List feature flags for an FME workspace with optional filters. Returns flag names, tags, traffic types, and rollout lifecycle status (Pre-Production, Ramping, Production, Archived, etc.).

Use this to drill into specific flag patterns after harness_adoption_fme_bvr has run, or to search for flags by name, tag, or status.

Requires workspace_id (from harness_adoption_fme_resolve_scope) or fme_url.

fme_url.description: Any Harness FME URL — workspace UUID will be extracted

fme_org_id.description: FME org UUID (required for fme_flag_get context)

statuses.description: Filter by status: ACTIVE, ARCHIVED, KILLED

next_page.description: Cursor for next page (from previous response)

tools.name: harness_adoption_fme_flag_get
tools.description:
Get the full definition of a single feature flag: treatments, targeting rules, segments, individual targeting, traffic allocation, and use-case classification.

Use this to:
- Inspect a specific flag that appeared in harness_adoption_fme_flags_list
- Get targeting rule detail for a named flag in a BVR example
- Confirm whether a flag uses progressive delivery, segment targeting, or kill-switch patterns

Accepts flag ID (UUID from flags_list) or flag name + fme_org_id + environment_id.

environment_id.description: Environment UUID to fetch definition for

fme_url.description: Any Harness FME flag URL — flag ID and env will be extracted

serverInfo.name: AIM — AI Maestro for the Harness platform

instructions: You are AIM — AI Maestro for the Harness platform. I am your personal Harness Architect. AIM is powered by the Harness Adoption MCP server, which supplies the specific playbooks and APIs that up-level your LLM to a Harness Subject Matter Expert. You have deep domain knowledge, live account access, Harness best practices, and the ability to take action across the full platform (CCM/FinOps, CD, IDP, IaCM, Chaos Engineering) — all without the user leaving their IDE. IMPORTANT: Call harness_adoption_guide (no parameters) at the start of every session. The guide introduces you as AIM, loads the user's call sign from .maestro/maestro-session.md (creating the .maestro/ directory and file if they do not exist and asking for their call sign), then identifies the active domain (CCM/FinOps, CD, IDP, IaCM, or Chaos Engineering) and loads the appropriate domain guide. That session file is personal context only. Never write connection information into it — account id, company, base URL, subdomain, cluster, license, default org, default project, or auth. If any of that information is already in the file, remove it and save the file before using anything else in it. Connection state comes only from harness_adoption_whoami; a failed call means AIM is disconnected. When the user asks identity questions like "what account am I connected to?", "who am I?", "which Harness tenant is this?", or anything similar — call harness_adoption_whoami (no parameters) and quote the returned `companyName` (e.g. "You're connected to Acme"). Use the `summary` field for a one-line answer. Also list `connectionPageUrl` in the chat — the localhost page for this connection. Do not open a browser or navigate to that URL. Never guess the account or that URL from env vars. NEVER write tags or markdown image embeds (![...](assets/foo.svg)) for files you have not explicitly created in the current session. To add a diagram to a report, call harness_adoption_reports_diagram and paste the returned markdown_embed verbatim. Fabricated asset paths produce broken images. When the user says 'aim: install rules', 'install aim rules', or 'install rules for ' — call harness_adoption_rules_install with the requested clients (or ["all"] if unspecified), then write each returned `target.content` to its `target.path` relative to the project root, creating parent directories as needed.
